en: present given in return; thank you gift

examples.ko: 결혼식에 와 주신 분들께 답례품을 드렸어요.
examples.en: We gave thank-you gifts to the people who came to the wedding.
I prepared small towels as return gifts for the first birthday party.

examples.ko: 답례품은 받는 분이 부담 없게 고르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to pick a return gift that doesn't burden the recipient.

examples.ko: 선물을 받고 감사의 뜻으로 답례품을 보냈어요.
examples.en: After receiving a gift, I sent a gift back as thanks.

examples.ko: 손님들에게 줄 답례품 포장을 하느라 바빴어요.
examples.en: I was busy wrapping the return gifts for the guests.

examples.ko: 답례품이 너무 비싸면 오히려 부담스러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the return gift is too expensive, it can actually feel burdensome.

explain: 결혼식, 돌잔치, 개업식 등에 와 준 사람이나 선물을 준 사람에게 감사의 뜻으로 주는 물건이에요. '답례'만 쓰면 인사나 보답하는 행동을 말하고, '답례품'은 그때 주는 물건을 가리켜요. 그냥 '선물'보다 보답이라는 느낌이 분명해요.
explain_en: It is a gift given as thanks to people who came to an event such as a wedding, first-birthday party or shop opening, or who gave you a present. '답례' alone refers to the act of returning thanks, while '답례품' is the item itself. It carries a clearer sense of repayment than a plain '선물'.

examples.en: I test-drove a new car over the weekend.
You can test-drive an electric car at the showroom.

examples.ko: 직접 시승하면 승차감을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you test-drive it yourself, you can feel how it rides.

examples.ko: 시승하지 않고 차를 사는 건 불안해요.
examples.en: Buying a car without test-driving it makes me uneasy.
I keep thinking about the car I test-drove yesterday.
Reporters test-drove the new model first.

explain: '차를 시승하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. 자주 '시승해 보다'의 꼴로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '타 보다'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It takes an object with '을/를', as in '차를 시승하다'. It often appears as '시승해 보다'. In everyday talk people also just say '타 보다'.

examples.en: How much is the gym's joining fee?
To join the club, you have to pay a joining fee.

examples.ko: 입회비는 처음에 한 번만 내면 돼요.
examples.en: You only have to pay the joining fee once at the beginning.

examples.ko: 입회비 삼만 원과 월회비 만 원을 냈어요.
examples.en: I paid a 30,000 won joining fee and a 10,000 won monthly fee.
There's an event where they discount the joining fee.
I paid the joining fee and got my membership card too.

explain: 모임이나 동호회, 운동 시설에 처음 들어갈 때 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 매달 내는 '월회비', 매년 내는 '연회비'와 구별해서 쓰고, '가입비'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the one-time money you pay when first joining a club, group or gym. Do not confuse it with 월회비 (monthly fee) or 연회비 (annual fee), and people also say 가입비.

en: appear in a show or film; perform on a program

examples.en: That actor appears in a new drama.
I appeared on a TV program yesterday.
It is a show where singers all perform together.

examples.ko: 그 배우가 주인공으로 출연한 영화가 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The film in which that actor starred as the lead became very popular.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 내년에 영화에 출연할 거라는 소식이 있어요.
examples.en: There is news that the singer will appear in a film next year.
My child said they want to appear in a commercial.

explain: 방송·영화·공연에 나오는 것을 말하고, 배우뿐 아니라 가수나 손님으로 나오는 사람에게도 써요. 보통 '~에 출연하다' 형태예요. 일상 대화에서는 '나오다'도 많이 써서 '그 드라마에 나와요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It covers appearing in a broadcast, film, or stage show, and applies to singers and guests as well as actors. It normally takes the form '~에 출연하다'. In casual talk, '나오다' is also common, as in '그 드라마에 나와요'.

examples.ko: 메일을 보낸 지 사흘이 지났는데 아직 회신이 없어요.
examples.en: It's been three days since I sent the email and there's no reply yet.
I'll be waiting for your answer.
Please send a reply by Friday at the latest.
I was glad to get a quick reply from the customer.

examples.ko: 회신 주소가 달라서 메일이 전달되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The reply address was different, so the email wasn't delivered.

examples.ko: 면접 결과는 이메일 회신으로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: We'll let you know the interview result by email reply.

explain: 메일 끝에 쓰는 '회신 부탁드립니다'처럼 회사에서 아주 자주 써요. 친구끼리는 '답장'이나 '답'이라고 해요. '회신을 주다', '회신을 받다', '회신을 기다리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is very common in work email, as in 회신 부탁드립니다. Friends say 답장 or 답 instead. Typical patterns are 회신을 주다, 회신을 받다, 회신을 기다리다.
